claims.reason: The public serializer derives useBlob from the selected options.Blob but instantiates global Blob. The probe confirmed a custom constructor is never called; without global Blob and Buffer the same supported local path throws. This is a conditional constructor contract defect, not a claim that every browser lacks these globals.

A caller-configured xsrfCookieName reaches the unescaped RegExp. A dotted valid name matches an unrelated cookie first. A malformed name containing a bracket and invalid range throws; a bare '[' alone does not necessarily throw. The prediction explicitly leaves attacker control and downstream security consequences unestablished, so no remote exploit credit is assigned.
README promises null on ignored parse failure, while the catch falls through to return the unchanged nonempty malformed string. Probe verified silent return and strict-mode rejection control.

The non-Buffer ArrayBufferView branch discards byteOffset and byteLength. Source tracing follows the transformed backing ArrayBuffer into HTTP's full Uint8Array conversion and req.end. A two-byte view of a four-byte backing buffer produced four fake-transport payload bytes. Production uncertainty metadata remains unchanged; real network transmission was not executed.

Object.keys includes own supplied keys, but mergeMap is a normal object. Its inherited toString replaces the supplied value with '[object Undefined]' in strict mode; an own JSON-parsed __proto__ selects a nonfunction and throws before configuration validation. Ordinary custom-key control is preserved. No prototype-pollution exploit is inferred.

Object.assign mutates the shared predicates object with per-call closures. A reentrant custom visitor replaced its helper functions; subsequent outer helpers.defaultVisitor appended the outer field to the inner form in the probe. No concurrent-thread assumption is needed.

The reverse-order notification loop has no per-listener guard. A later subscribed throwing callback prevents earlier subscribers from being notified, skips _listeners cleanup and rejects the ignored then promise. Probe observed all three effects. Scope is a shared token with a throwing subscriber, not ordinary cancellation with all callbacks well-behaved.

The aborted handler does not test totalResponseBytes or enabled maxContentLength and always reports a size-limit failure if not already rejected. A zero-body fake stream abortion with disabled -1 limit emitted 'maxContentLength size of -1 exceeded'.

The module declares request but never req. AbortController's event selects construction with req, raising ReferenceError before rejection or request.abort. A fake signal fired after send confirmed the request abort was not reached. Pre-aborted signals may reject during Promise construction rather than leave a sent request; the finding's can-leave-running wording is correctly conditional.

withCredentials alone selects the current document's XSRF cookie and copies it into a request header even when the target is cross-origin; source then installs that header and sends. The probe established this local primitive with same-origin false and a false-withCredentials negative control. The reported disclosure is explicitly conditional on caller URL influence and permitted credentialed CORS. Real browser CORS, remote attacker reach and deployment impact remain unverified; this verdict does not remove the saved support_unverified flag or certify an actual exploit.

The adapter checks request data.length when deleting the response's content-encoding. Buffer.alloc(0) is truthy and retains length zero. With a compressed nonempty response the fake transport returned raw compressed bytes and removed the header; a nonempty-request control decompressed the same response.

UTF-8 text conversion strips a BOM into request variable data but returns convertedData. A valid base64 data URI probe retained U+FEFF; the ordinary HTTP text path assigns the stripped string to the actual returned response variable.
